thread:
maya: thinking about a small, minimally invasive protocol for geo lease swaps + cache transfer when a primary fails. need something simple we can ship as an MVP before the full handshake RFC. goals: correctness on failover, respect data residency, avoid long global locks. :thinking:

joel: short answer: 4-step swap with explicit handoff tokens. keep metadata small, rely on idempotent ops. rough sketch: REQUEST_SWAP -> PREPARE -> TRANSFER -> ACTIVATE. each step has a token and monotonic counter.

sophie: two constraints to keep in mind: 1) if residency says 'EU-only', we must never copy KV to non-EU hosts, so TRANSFER might be a no-op (remote proxy only). 2) any token exchange must be auditable for compliance.

ana: practically, the PREPARE step should snapshot lease info + KV TTLs and write to an append-only audit log (KMS-signed). prefer KMS envelope for tokens. if TRANSFER blocked by residency, the new primary should run in proxy-mode and rehydrate locally from allowed replicas only.

joel: here is the minimal message flow I had in mind (pseudocode):

```
// initiator = CurrentPrimary, target = CandidatePrimary
REQUEST_SWAP(initiator->target): {tenant, lease_id, epoch}
PREPARE(target->initiator): {accept, transfer_token}
TRANSFER(initiator->target): {transfer_batch, transfer_token}
ACTIVATE(target->all): {lease_id, activation_ts, signature}
```

Notes: - transfer_token binds PREPARE+TRANSFER; tokens signed by KMS. - transfer_batch can be empty if residency prevents copy; still send metadata. - ACTIVATE broadcast lets routers switch without needing global lock.

maya: nice. what about races where two candidates try to seize?

joel: monotonic epoch + single-writer guarantee from the current primary. candidate must present REQUEST_SWAP with epoch > current. initiator refuses if it already handed off. Idempotency: TRANSFER includes sequence numbers, so retries are safe.

sophie: also TTLs: KV entries must carry origin-region TTL and a 'grace-until' to avoid re-serving stale data after activation. propose a guard: target must respect origin TTLs and not extend them.

ana: audit footprint: every step writes a compact entry to the audit store: {tenant, step, token_hash, region, ts}. logs signed and retained per customer retention policy.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/prod rollout of swap-handler v0.1 at 2026-04-01T04:00Z :rocket: 

maya: OK next actions: 1) joel/ana to draft the token shape + KMS signing API. 2) sophie to write residency-mode matrix (copy/proxy/no-copy). 3) i'll pull a short test plan for canary (simulate primary crash + dual-candidate). aim to ship v0.1 in 2 sprints. :+1: 

joel: i'll put a draft PR with the pseudocode and unit tests. will link to this thread.

sophie: one follow-up: add a post-swap validation job that verifies routers have switched and no write-back to origin is happening. small metric: per-tenant swap-success-rate and stale-read-rate.

maya: agreed. thanks all. closing this thread, will open RFC follow-up if we hit edgecases in the canary.
